Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating stable preferences from current intent, then learning their interaction. [BLSI (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0020025524010417) combines short-term self-attention, long-term graph encoding and adaptive gating, although its multiple behavior types exceed this task’s available signals. More directly applicable, [hierarchical long/short-term modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) builds multiple long-term interest vectors through dynamic routing, extracts recent intent with self-attention, retrieves the long-term interest most similar to that intent, and integrates time encoding. [GRELA (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13315) combines rotary-enhanced linear attention, a local preference operation and SiLU gating to distinguish local interests from sustained preference shifts.

The 2026 direction extends this separation across temporal scales. [MIMAR-SRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intent across contextual windows, with prototype/sequence contrastive learning and perturbation-based robustness. [DiffLSRec](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v318/wang26a.html) treats long-term preferences as a diffusion prior and short-term intent as adaptive denoising guidance; its authors report improvements on three Amazon datasets, without establishing gains on this benchmark.

Architecture inference for the constrained SASRec task: retain its sequence encoder, add a recent-window intent branch and several attention-pooled historical interest vectors, then let recent intent select relevant historical interests. Learn a gate conditioned on both representations, their agreement, history length and observed time gaps. This uses available histories and timestamps without requiring unobserved traits. Compare against SASRec and fixed fusion using the common macro validation HR@10; these papers motivate the design but do not establish its benchmark benefit.

---

Multi-negative training is a well-supported SASRec experiment. [gSASRec (2023; IJCAI 2024 summary)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) combines multiple negatives with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence; authors recommend 128–256 negatives and calibration parameter t=0.75, balancing effectiveness against compute. Sampled-softmax cross-entropy offers a practical alternative. The [RecSys 2025 LogQ repository](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides SASRec implementations for uniform, in-batch, mixed sampling and alternative sampling-probability corrections. These support comparing objectives and samplers separately, rather than assuming harder negatives explain improvements.

Hard-negative selection needs false-negative controls. [CATS (2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) uses item clusters and adaptive Thompson sampling, progressively reducing sampling from the positive item’s cluster while exploring neighboring clusters and the wider catalog. Its premise: the hardest nearby items can include plausible positives. A [2024 comparative study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) also finds dataset-dependent trade-offs: random sampling favors head items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at lower aggregate accuracy. Neither finding establishes gains specifically for Electronics.

Practical hypothesis for this benchmark: compare single-negative BCE against uniform multi-negative sampled softmax and gBCE; then test a modest hard-negative mixture. Proposed safeguards—not established optimal settings—include excluding padding, the current positive and observed training-history items; deduplicating candidates; and retaining random negatives instead of selecting only maximum-score items. Use training interactions or learned embeddings for controls, without unavailable attributes or held-out labels. Select exclusively by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, reporting Electronics separately; larger training margins alone provide no evidence of ranking generalization.

---

Recent work supports separating sequential transitions from general item similarity. MQSA-TED (WSDM 2024) combines short/long attention queries with distillation of global item-to-item transitions into embeddings—an applicable extension to SASRec without pretrained text models ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056)). *Revisiting Graph Projections* (2025) offers a simpler alternative: infer complementary recommendations using a directed, weighted item graph projected from historical user–item interactions, explicitly addressing sparse, noisy observations ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209)). Earlier SCG-SPRe explicitly models substitutable and complementary relations separately, providing architectural precedent for distinct relation channels ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3464302)). These results motivate directional scoring, but observed transitions alone do not establish functional complementarity.

Text-aware work also warns against treating semantic similarity as sufficient: ST2SI (COLING 2025) emphasizes learning item transitions and aligning text with item IDs; its pretrained-LLM implementation falls outside this task’s constraints ([paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/)). A lightweight experimental adaptation—not a reported result—would blend SASRec scores with a smoothed, recency-weighted directed transition graph, using separate source/target embeddings to preserve asymmetry. Locally fitted title/description TF-IDF/SVD features or randomly initialized token embeddings could share statistical strength across sparse items; train distinct projections for transition prediction and semantic similarity rather than declaring similar items complementary. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses positive next items and sampled negatives. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
